root_idea.summary: A semantic orientation of flowing, moving, or spreading across a surface or space.
root_idea.development: The evidence develops from water running over the earth to traveling through the land, the movement of shade, and striped or streaked forms whose lines are likened to flowing movement. Some derivatives extend this idea to roaming speech or mischief.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The imperative QAC form is normalized to the Form I perfect citation headword سَاحَ.
The feminine plural Quran form is presented under the normalized active-participle citation form سَائِحٌ.
The masculine plural Quran form is grouped with the same normalized active-participle headword.

senses.definition: To travel or move about through the land.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic imperative, used with في الأرض to command or permit movement through the land.

senses.definition: One who travels or journeys through the land; one who goes forth.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic feminine plural may be interpreted as women who leave their country or homes for God; another Quranic interpretation takes the form as referring to those journeying for war or the pursuit of knowledge.
The Quranic plural forms are explained as fasters, including, in reported interpretations, those who observe obligatory or continual fasts or who remain in mosques while fasting.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of water: to run upon the surface of the earth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The subject is water or another flowing liquid.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Devotional journeying through the land; by religious analogy, fasting as a form of Muslim siyāḥah.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression لا سِيَاحَةَ فِي الإِسْلَامِ is explained in several ways, including prohibition of devotional wandering, desert withdrawal, or wandering to spread mischief.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of shade: to move or turn from side to side or from place to place.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension of movement is used with الظلّ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make water flow.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported Form II usage, attributed as a primary or proper signification in the lexical discussion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To talk much or at length.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative Form II usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a garment or piece of cloth: to make it striped or variegated with stripes.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative Form II usage describing diversified cloth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make a river or rivulet flow.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form IV causative construction with a river or stream as object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a horse: to expose its penis from the prepuce.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An animal-specific figurative usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a horse: to let its tail hang loosely.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The spelling is disputed in the lexical tradition, with أَشَاحَ also reported by some authorities.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a belly: to become large and wide and approach the ground through fatness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of an animal or person whose enlarged belly hangs low.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a state or condition: to become free from straitness or distress.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative usage applied to a person's or thing's condition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become rent, split, or broken in several places; of dawn, to break.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A cave narrative applies the verb to rock becoming impelled and riven, but that application is transmitted with the alternative form اِنْصَاخَتْ by some authorities.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Running water, especially external water flowing over the earth, including the water of rivers and valleys.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used substantivally and also as an epithet of water.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A striped garment, such as a cloak, mantle, or striped burd.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative noun based on the appearance of flowing or running lines.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An itinerant, rover, or frequent traveler.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A derived nominal referring to one who repeatedly travels through the land.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Swift horses.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This interpretation is conditional on retaining سَائِحَاتٌ rather than treating the form as a possible transcription of سَابِحَاتٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The planets.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported figurative interpretation of the same conditionally retained form; it is likewise subject to the possible reading سَابِحَاتٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place of journeying or religious travel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The singular of مَسَايِحُ in the lexical discussion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The part of the head between the temples and the forehead, where the hair grows.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized plural usage recorded in poetic vocabulary.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Striped or streaked; applied especially to garments and to marked or streaked locusts, and also to a bird.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Garment stripes may alternate white and black; locusts may be marked with black, yellow, and white streaks.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A wild ass, named for the stripe dividing its belly from its side; also an ass with a white streak on its rump.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A lexicalized animal epithet based on distinctive streaking.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A road whose tracks or wheel-ruts are visible.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative application likening the visible tracks to stripes.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who goes about calumniating, spreading mischief, and corrupting relations among people.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A pejorative intensive noun; its plural is مَسَايِيحُ.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Travel through the land and devotional siyāḥah, including the fasting analogy.
Rending or breaking, with a disputed cave application.
One who journeys through the land.

cautions: The Quranic active-participle forms have interpretive alternatives: fasting, or journeying and leaving homes for God. The supplied Quran locations are secure, but contextual English glosses do not by themselves resolve the alternatives.
The reported application of اِنْسَاحَتْ to the cave rock is retained only as a conditional Classical usage because an alternative transmission uses اِنْصَاخَتْ.
The interpretations of سَائِحَاتٌ as swift horses and planets are conditional on the form not being a transcription of سَابِحَاتٌ.
